executive_summary: GBP/CAD trades at 1.86543 (gated price-store close, 2026-09-03), meaning one pound buys 1.86543 Canadian dollars; a rising pair is sterling strengthening against the loonie. The pair has fallen 1.15% over one month, gained a negligible 0.22% over three, gained 2.34% over six and lost 0.47% over twelve — a cross that has round-tripped a year and is currently rolling over from a July peak, sitting at the 57th percentile of its 52-week closing range of 1.816 to 1.90211. The dominant bilateral narrative is a collision between the widest stable carry advantage sterling holds against any G10 currency that is not a funding currency — 150 basis points, frozen by two near-certain holds inside the tactical window — and the cleanest terms-of-trade and sovereign-quality asymmetry available in the G10: a net energy importer running a 2.8%-of-GDP current account deficit with the widest gilt-Bund spread since the 2022 mini-Budget, against a net energy exporter that just posted its largest current account surplus since 2005 and is one of only two AAA-rated G7 sovereigns. Three bilateral differentials diverge materially from what either standalone dossier would imply: the base dossier's bearish Policy & Rates stance is built almost entirely on the 2026-09-10 ECB hike and the 2026-09-16 FOMC hike compressing sterling's euro and dollar advantages, and neither leg exists in this cross, so most published sterling rate-bearishness simply does not transmit here; the quote dossier's Neutral CAD conceals a speculative short at the 12th percentile covering at roughly six times the rate of sterling's, which is a pair-directional flow the standalone view cannot see; and the two central banks' forecast rounds collide on 2026-10-28, testing opposite legs of the thesis on the same afternoon. The settled verdict is Bearish on both horizons at conviction 2 — tactical net score -0.2428, strategic -0.1212 — and we publish it with the caveat that the strategic call sits only 0.0212 beyond the Neutral boundary, with Policy & Rates at +0.1248 and External Balance at -0.1235 within 0.0013 of cancelling each other outright. The price payload corroborates the tactical direction — lower highs since 7 July, a break below both the 50-day and 100-day averages on 2 September, and realised volatility compressed to 3.22% — but that corroboration was deliberately withheld from the scoring pass and is reported here as market context, not as evidence for the stance.

market_context.valuation_assessment: There is no free PPP source for this cross, so valuation is assessed on relative BIS REERs, a labelled proxy. Sterling's REER of 111.41 (June 2026) is the third-highest in the G10+SGD set, while Canada's 95.71 is the second-cheapest behind only the yen — a 16.4% relative premium for sterling, the widest gap sterling carries against any currency in the set other than the yen. Equalising the two REER levels implies GBP/CAD at approximately 1.6167, some 15.4% below spot; that is a relative-standing arithmetic exercise, not a tradeable target, and this premium has persisted for nearly two years without mean-reverting. Canada's REER has fallen 3.41 points over twelve months versus sterling's 2.73, so the gap has widened rather than closed. What is priced into 1.86543 is a persistent, institutionalised Canadian growth-and-trade discount against sterling's carry premium, with neither side assuming resolution of the US-Canada tariff conflict or a UK fiscal accident. Valuation caps how far the pair can extend rather than providing a tactical trigger — a structural headwind, not a catalyst.

market_context.recent_regime: The pair spent July at its highs and August coiling beneath them. From 3 August to 1 September the entire range was 1.87435 to 1.89552 (roughly 210 pips, three ATRs) with 20-day realised falling to 3.22% against a 60-day baseline of 4.28% — a compression regime. Within it, structure quietly deteriorated: each rally high was lower than the last, the late-August bounce to 1.8897 failed 25 pips below the 5 August high, and the pair closed below its 50-day for the entire month. The regime broke on 2 September, opening at 1.87833, trading to 1.88296 and selling 171 pips to close at 1.86686, taking out the 100-day average, then extending to 1.86109 intraday on 3 September and closing at 1.86543 on the 200-day. The dominant narrative through the compression was two central banks going nowhere while Canadian data ran hot and the Canadian speculative short bled out — and the resolution, when it came, came lower.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: Bank Rate at 3.75% against the BoC overnight target at 2.25% gives a +150bp annualised carry to a long GBP/CAD position. The carry-to-vol ratio is 0.31 using the payload's 3-month estimated ATM implied vol of 4.899%; because that vol input is a measured floor running low by a median 14.4%, the corrected ratio is more likely 0.26 to 0.28. That is a working carry cross but not a spectacular one — fifteen times better than cable's 0.02 against the dollar and less than half of sterling's 0.78 against the franc, close to the Canadian dollar's own best carry leg, CAD/CHF at 0.41. Forward points are derived, not quoted, from two methods (policy differential and observed futures roll) that agree to within 14 pips at six months. Carry is working in level terms and is not the reason to own this pair — it is the single mechanical support under GBP/CAD, fully expressed in a spot rate at the 57th percentile of its closing range, and the tradeable question is whether it survives the roughly 65% probability of a 2026 BoC hike currently embedded in Canadian OIS, which is scored strategically and is why the strategic Policy & Rates contribution is the largest single positive anywhere in this analysis.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Bank Rate at 3.75% against a Bank of Canada overnight target of 2.25% gives sterling a 150 basis point policy advantage, the third widest of the sterling crosses behind the franc and the yen. The decisive tactical observation is that nothing scheduled inside four weeks can change that number. The gated calendar has the Bank of Canada deciding on 2026-09-02 with a 3% hike probability and all 35 Reuters-polled economists forecasting no change, and the Bank of England on 2026-09-17 with roughly +7 basis points priced and 56 of 64 economists expecting no change for the rest of 2026. Both are near-certain holds, so the differential enters and leaves the tactical window at 150 basis points. This is also where the base dossier's bearish rate stance must be corrected for the cross: that stance rests almost entirely on the 2026-09-10 ECB hike and the 2026-09-16 FOMC hike compressing sterling's euro and dollar advantages, and neither leg exists in GBP/CAD. Stripped of the dollar and euro channels, sterling's rate story against Canada is a stable, wide and positive carry. The residual tactical content is the ten-year comparison, and it is unusable at face value: both legs in the payload are monthly series as of 2026-06-01, showing a 137.6bp differential, while the dossiers carry live late-August levels implying approximately +140bp. The direction agrees, the level is stale, and the widening is a UK fiscal premium rather than a policy premium, scored in Factor 8.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the two curves are priced with opposite asymmetries and that is the strategic edge in this cross. Sterling's next move has been pushed into 2027 — the market prices essentially nothing for 2026 after the collapse from an 87.2% cumulative December hike probability at end-July — so there is very little BoE hawkishness left to disappoint. Canada is the mirror image: roughly 65% of a Bank of Canada hike by end-2026 is embedded in Canadian OIS, 47% of the Reuters panel expects at least one increase by end-Q2 2027, and National Bank and Scotiabank both forecast 2.75% by December against a BMO, CIBC, RBC and TD consensus of no change. The Bank's own Q2 2026 Market Participants Survey has the median policy rate at 2.25% through January 2027 and only 2.50% in March 2027, a one-to-two-quarter wedge against market pricing. If the differential compresses as priced, it goes from 150 to 125 or 100bp and the pair loses carry; if the Canadian hike pricing is marked out instead, the differential holds at 150 and the pair gains relative to the forward. The evidence favours the second: CPI-trim is 1.9% and CPI-median 2.0% with the entire headline-core gap attributable to gasoline up 25.7% y/y, wage growth has decelerated to 2.8% from 3.3%, and Statistics Canada's July advance GDP estimate was 0.0% before Section 338 duties took effect. The dated tests are the BoC decisions of 2026-10-28 (with Monetary Policy Report) and 2026-12-09. The offset, and the reason confidence is only 52, is that the BoE's own reaction function is symmetric, with three standing hawks voting again at the 2026-11-05 Monetary Policy Report and a dovish wing arguing for cuts, so sterling's side of the differential is not immune either.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The growth differential has moved sharply against sterling on the most recent prints. Canada grew 3.3% annualised in Q2 2026, the fastest since early 2023 and 80bp above the BoC's own 2.5% projection, while the UK grew 0.4% q/q, roughly 1.6% annualised, and 1.2% y/y. On the labour side the trajectories are opposed: Canadian unemployment fell to 6.4% in July, a two-year low and a third consecutive monthly decline, with employment up 75,000, while UK unemployment is 4.9% and up 0.2pp on the year with payrolled employees down 210,000 and vacancies at 705,000, the lowest since early 2021. Canada also carries the better surprise ledger, with five upside beats against three misses in August including a C$5.3bn current account beat, whereas the UK data set is self-contradicting — August composite PMI at 52.5 and services at 52.8 against retail sales down 0.5% and CBI distributive trades at -48. On inflation the comparison cuts the other way but weakly: UK core is 2.6% and services 3.4% against Canadian CPI-trim at 1.9% and CPI-median at 2.0%, so sterling has more underlying inflation to defend its rate, but the base dossier's own reading is that this is disinflating rather than accelerating. The transmission is asymmetric sensitivity: with the Canadian rate market carrying 65% of a hike, a Canadian labour or CPI beat moves this cross harder than an equivalent UK print, because the UK curve has already stopped listening.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Extend the horizon and both economies deteriorate for different reasons, and the differential closes rather than widens. Canada's Q2 print describes a quarter that ended in June; Statistics Canada's July advance estimate was 0.0%, recorded before the 2026-08-22 Section 338 duties and before Canada's 2026-09-08 counter-measures, and the BoC's July projection has full-year 2026 growth at just 0.7%, which after a 3.3% annualised Q2 implies materially sub-trend second-half outcomes. Against that, the UK carries its own slow deterioration: 1.2% y/y growth, a loosening labour market, real regular pay growth of only 0.5%, and an MPC member describing an economy drifting toward deficient demand. On inflation the two converge from opposite directions — Canadian headline at 3.0% falls toward 2.0% core as the 25.7% gasoline base effect rolls off, while UK headline at 2.9% is pushed up by imported energy the committee has said it will look through. Neither disinflation path is a currency signal on its own. The honest strategic read is that a 0.7% Canadian growth path and a roughly 1.0-1.2% UK path, both with decelerating wages and a central bank unable to raise the nominal rate to defend a real rate, is a wash. Assigning direction here would be manufacturing a view from two symmetric downgrades, and the framework's own instruction is that Neutral is a real answer.

factors.horizon_split: The stance moves from Bearish to Neutral because the two horizons trade different quarters. The tactical window trades the Canadian Q2 beat and 6.4% unemployment against a self-contradicting UK data set; the strategic window trades the July 0.0% Canadian flash and the Bank's own 0.7% full-year call against a UK labour market loosening on the same timetable — two symmetric downgrades that cancel. factors.weight_adjustment_reason: GBP/CAD is a low risk-sensitivity cross: both legs are mildly pro-cyclical G10 currencies with no safe-haven leg, so the risk beta largely nets out and what survives is the commodity channel, scored in Factor 5 rather than double-counted here.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the classification the framework calls low risk sensitivity, and the current regime does not change it. Both currencies are mildly risk-positive with no haven leg: sterling strengthens in risk-on with less beta than the Antipodeans, and the Canadian dollar carries a comparable mild positive beta anchored by its US linkage, with USD/CAD's normal correlation to the S&P 500 only -0.2 to -0.3, roughly half the Antipodean sensitivity. With the VIX at 14.51 on 2026-08-27, down 3.70 points on the month and near the 2026 low, US IG at 79bp and HY at 263bp after 21bp of monthly tightening, the global backdrop is unambiguously supportive — but supportive of both legs roughly equally, which is precisely why it yields no pair signal. The one genuine asymmetry is domestic equity: the FTSE 250 has underperformed the FTSE 100 by roughly 10pp, while the TSX Composite fell 1.02% on 2026-08-31 on tariff-specific pressure — those cancel. The residual risk channel that would be directional is oil, since sterling is an energy importer and CAD an exporter, but oil is currently rising on a supply constraint rather than a demand impulse, severing the ordinary risk-beta link and routing the whole effect into terms of trade.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the risk factor remains non-directional for this cross and its informational content decays further, which is why the weight is cut to 0.03. Both dossiers reach the same conclusion independently: sterling's dominant risk exposure becomes idiosyncratic and fiscal once the 2026-10-28 Budget enters the window, and the Canadian dollar's risk beta is severed by an oil regime that is supply-driven rather than demand-driven. Two currencies whose global risk betas have both been overwritten by domestic idiosyncratic risk produce a cross with no beta to extract. The tail scenarios confirm rather than resolve this. A Hormuz reopening would be risk-positive and simultaneously remove sterling's terms-of-trade tax and Canada's windfall, so its net pair effect is small and ambiguous. A Hormuz re-escalation would be risk-negative and would help CAD through revenue while taxing sterling through the import bill — directional but a commodity effect. A generic equity correction as the Fed hikes into record valuations would hurt both legs, probably sterling slightly more given its higher broad-dollar beta, scored in Factor 10. None of these establishes a strategic risk-appetite stance.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Speculators are short both legs, which normally mutes a cross signal, but the two shorts are of very different sizes and are unwinding at very different speeds, and that asymmetry is the tactical content. Sterling's headline non-commercial net is -44,500 contracts on the 2026-08-28 release, roughly the 30th percentile, well inside the -80,000 threshold the base brief calls stretched, with leveraged funds already net long 40,670. The Canadian dollar's combined leveraged-fund and asset-manager net short is -131,035 contracts at the 2026-08-25 reference date, around the 12th percentile, with dealers warehousing the other side at net long 124,930. The covering rates differ by an order of magnitude: sterling has covered roughly 10,100 contracts in a week, while the Canadian dollar covered 65,515 contracts, a third of the position, in a single fortnight — into the week the 50% Section 338 duties took effect, the signature of a stale short being stopped out. Netting the two legs, the more crowded and more actively squeezing short is the quote currency, so the mechanical flow inside four weeks buys Canadian dollars faster than it buys sterling and pushes the cross lower.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months positioning decays from flow into stock, and on the stock measure the asymmetry narrows but does not reverse. A residual CAD speculative short of 131,035 contracts, 39.8% of open interest net and 64.9% of gross shorts, remains a genuine cushion under the quote currency, corroborated by real-money flow: foreign investors bought a record C$80.8bn of Canadian government bonds in Q2 2026, the same quarter the current account swung to surplus. Sterling's residual short is smaller, concentrated in asset managers whose positions are hedge-driven and slow to unwind, alongside leveraged funds already long — a thinner cushion into the 2026-10-28 Budget. The structural sterling flow that matters strategically is the opposite of supportive: UK pension/insurance hedge-ratio behaviour and roughly 25-30% foreign ownership of gilts are the channels that turned the 2022 fiscal event into a currency event. Netting, the quote currency has more cushion and better real-money flow, the base currency has less cushion and a live fiscal transmission channel, so the factor stays bearish, though weakly — shrinking open interest on both legs reduces squeeze mechanics over a multi-month window.

Meanwhile the sterling short is no longer the cushion it looks like, because the covering has run for six consecutive weeks and leveraged funds at 15.9% of OI are no longer the marginal buyer — so a hawkish UK surprise would find the pair with less resistance above than the headline net short implies.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: This is the defining bilateral asymmetry of GBP/CAD: a net energy importer running a 2.8%-of-GDP current account deficit against a net energy exporter that has just posted its largest current account surplus since 2005, with the same closed Strait of Hormuz driving both. The framework's own guidance is to boost this factor for commodity-versus-non-commodity pairs, and the effect here is unusually clean because the tariff regime explicitly carves out energy.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The external accounts of the two economies moved in opposite directions in the same quarter and for the same reason. The UK ran a current account deficit of GBP 22.1bn in Q1 2026, 2.8% of GDP, with the goods deficit widening GBP 4.0bn to GBP 59.5bn while the offsetting services surplus fell GBP 1.2bn — and the headline narrowing came from a GBP 8.0bn primary income swing rather than trade. Canada swung from a C$8.3bn Q1 deficit to a C$8.8bn Q2 surplus, the first since 2022 and the largest since 2005, on record energy and auto exports, against a C$3.5bn consensus. The driver is the same shock viewed from both ends: UK NBP front-month gas settled at 161.02p/therm on 2026-08-26 and around 165p on 2026-08-28, 18-21% above the BoE's own 136-pence July conditioning assumption and roughly 43% higher on the year, while Brent was US$90.135 and WTI US$85.446 on 2026-08-31. The framework's direction rules put oil up as negative for sterling and strongly positive for CAD, and NBP gas up as negative for sterling. Both rules point the same way for this cross. Critically, the Section 338 tariff regime carved out energy, potash, fish and critical minerals, so Canada's largest export category trades on global prices rather than bilateral politics. The direct bilateral trade channel is immaterial: IMF DOTS shows UK exports to Canada of US$8.9bn against imports of US$8.4bn in 2024, a US$0.5bn net balance that is a rounding error.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: This is the highest-confidence stance in the analysis and it carries the largest strategic weight after Policy & Rates. The mechanism is a multi-quarter income transfer running in one direction: the UK must sell sterling to buy energy at prices 18-21% above its own central bank's conditioning assumption, while Canada receives that same transfer, and the northern hemisphere heating season falls inside the horizon with European storage refill competing against Asian LNG buyers. The EIA projects Brent averaging US$87 for 2026 with roughly 0.6mb/d of Hormuz disruption persisting through end-2027, a structural supply regime rather than a spike. The composition of the UK deficit is worse than the headline: the goods deficit that energy drives is widening and the financial-services surplus that offsets it is shrinking, and post-Brexit trade barriers have structurally reduced trade openness. Canada's counterweights are real and are why confidence is 65 rather than 80: the Section 338 duties cover 554 lines and US$20bn, 5.2% of the US$382bn shipped south in 2025, escalating to 50% on autos, trucks, parts and steel from 2027-01-01, and the WCS-WTI heavy differential of roughly US$12/bbl caps Canadian realisation of any Brent rally. But the tariffs do not touch the commodity complex, Canada's capital account is being funded by record foreign sovereign bond demand rather than depreciation, and its Q1 current account of -0.87% of GDP was already better than the UK's -2.84% before the Q2 swing to surplus.

Terms-of-trade effects transmit with a lag of quarters rather than weeks, so over four weeks the gas and crude levels are headlines while over one to six months they are a measurable income transfer that shows up in both countries' balance of payments and in the UK energy price cap. net_commodity_exposure.base_commodity_profile: Sterling is a net energy importer with no offsetting commodity export complex. UK NBP front-month gas at 161-165 pence per therm in the last week of August is 18-21% above the BoE's own 136-pence July conditioning assumption and roughly 43% higher on the year, and the UK runs a 2.8%-of-GDP current account deficit with a widening goods deficit. Direction rules: oil up is negative for GBP, natural gas up is negative for GBP, gold up is broadly neutral.
net_commodity_exposure.quote_commodity_profile: The Canadian dollar is a petro-currency and broad commodity exporter. Brent at US$90.135 and WTI at US$85.446 on 2026-08-31 feed directly into export revenue, the BoC's July deliberations recorded aluminium and copper benefiting from supply constraints, and Canada posted a C$8.8bn Q2 current account surplus on record energy and auto exports. Direction rules: oil up is strongly positive for CAD, and Canadian energy is explicitly exempt from the Section 338 tariff regime.
net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: Apply the framework's direction rules leg by leg. Oil up: sterling takes a clear negative through a widening import bill on a 2.8%-of-GDP deficit, while the Canadian dollar takes a strong positive through export revenue that the tariffs do not touch. Netting a negative base against a strongly positive quote gives a falling pair, bearish GBP/CAD. Natural gas up: NBP gas up is a direct negative for sterling, while Canada is a net gas exporter and LNG participant, neutral-to-mildly-positive for the quote leg. Netting again gives a falling pair. There is no commodity in the set on which sterling is the beneficiary and the Canadian dollar the payer, so the two rules reinforce rather than offset — one of the few crosses in the G10 where commodity netting is unambiguous in a single direction. The bounded offset is the tariff regime, a trade-policy negative for the quote leg worth 5.2% of its US exports, with energy carved out — that limits magnitude but does not reverse sign.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_up_10pct: Brent from roughly US$90 to US$99 with NBP gas dragged higher on the same Hormuz constraint: sterling's import bill deteriorates on an already 2.8%-of-GDP deficit while Canadian export revenue and current account surplus both improve. Net effect strongly bearish GBP/CAD, the largest single-variable move available in this analysis.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_down_10pct: Brent from roughly US$90 to US$81 on a credible Hormuz reopening: the UK energy import bill collapses while Bank Rate stays at 3.75% (the single most sterling-positive combination available per the base dossier), and Canada's terms-of-trade windfall and current account surplus both reverse. Net effect bullish GBP/CAD, and the cleanest way this analysis is wrong.
net_commodity_exposure.dominant_commodity_driver: Crude oil, with UK NBP natural gas a close and partly independent second. Crude drives the quote leg's revenue and current account directly; NBP gas drives the base leg's import bill and the BoE's own conditioning assumption. Because both are hostage to the same Strait of Hormuz constraint, they currently move together and their effects on this cross compound rather than diversify.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Both central banks have published deliberately two-sided guidance, and two symmetric reaction functions produce no pair signal. The BoE's 29 July minutes held 6-3 with Greene, Mann and Pill voting for 4.00%, said risks to inflation are tilted to the upside relative to the July projection, but justified the hold on financial conditions tightening being sufficient insurance, with Ramsden explicitly two-way and Taylor openly dovish. The BoC's July statement judged the current rate appropriate while ready to adjust, and its Summary of Deliberations agreed to look through direct oil effects while committing not to let higher oil prices become persistent inflation — a hawkish commitment device attached to a dovish assessment, with a disclosed range of views. Sequencing favours neither leg: the BoC decides 2026-09-02, fifteen days before the BoE on 2026-09-17, but with a 3% hike probability and 35 of 35 economists at hold, the tradeable content is a press-conference tone that is genuinely a coin flip. Both institutions are highly credible with aligned pricing, which is the definition of no tactical edge.

On the Canadian side, 2026-10-28 carries a Monetary Policy Report at which the Bank must publish numbers behind a market pricing roughly 65% of a 2026 hike, against its own Q2 Market Participants Survey median of 2.25% through January 2027 and 2.50% only in March 2027. A downgraded forecast would mark that pricing out and weaken CAD. On the sterling side, the 2026-11-05 Monetary Policy Report is a full forecast round at which three standing hawks vote again, with 2027 pay settlements named as decisive; incoming evidence leans dovish — private-sector regular pay 2.8%, DMP year-ahead wage expectations 3.4% and three-year CPI expectations 2.8% — which would weaken sterling on the same timetable. Both banks are credible communicators with symmetric functions facing dovish-leaning resolutions within a week of each other — two wide but unbiased distributions overlapping, and the correct pair stance is Neutral even though this is the third-largest strategic weight.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Tactical weight adjusted from default 0.05 to 0.07: both legs carry a live, dated policy-event risk inside four weeks rather than the usual one-sided calendar — the composition of Canada's retaliatory tariff list taking effect 2026-09-08 was unpublished at the valuation date, and the UK carries a dense scheduled data cluster plus the MPC's annual QT vote on 2026-09-17. tactical.bilateral_analysis: Inside four weeks the only genuinely unpriced binary on either leg sits on the quote side. Canada's retaliatory tariffs take effect on 2026-09-08 on approximately US$20bn of US goods at rates of 15-50% covering steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, electronics and motorcycles, and the product-level list had not been published at the valuation date. Prime Minister Carney called the step reluctant precisely because it raises Canadian costs, and dollar-for-dollar retaliation is proportionally heavier on an economy roughly one tenth the size of its counterpart. Against that, the UK tactical calendar is dense but genuinely non-binary: scheduled releases with published consensus, the Budget date fixed since 31 July, and a political transition to PM Burnham and Chancellor Healey absorbed with sterling and gilts stable. A scheduled data cluster against an unpublished tariff list is an asymmetry favouring the pair rising. Confidence is only 50 because the asymmetry is small, the tariff scope is bounded at 5.2% of Canadian exports with energy exempt, and a hawkish UK surprise could easily overwhelm it.

The UK Autumn Budget on 2026-10-28 arrives with an accompanying OBR forecast, delivered by a Chancellor appointed three weeks before the date was set under a PM three months into office, with the OBR's March headroom of GBP 9.9bn almost certainly consumed by a 39bp year-on-year rise in the ten-year gilt at roughly GBP 2.5bn of debt service per 0.25pp. The distribution is skewed to the downside for sterling because fiscal rules cap the good outcome while a 30-year gilt at 5.73-5.76% amplifies the bad one, and the market's base case is continuity — as it also was in September 2022. Canada's strategic event risk is more severe in kind but far better understood: Section 338 has no expiry, escalation to 50% on autos/trucks/parts/steel is dated 2027-01-01, and the USMCA six-year review was triggered 2026-07-01 with Canada absent from the US-Mexico track — bad but bounded at 5.2% of bilateral exports with energy exempt, already in spot, and the 2026-11-03 midterms are a dated potential circuit-breaker that would be quote-positive.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: For most crosses this is a background factor; for GBP/CAD it is the widest sovereign-quality gap available in the G10 — a AA/AA-/Aa2-Aa3 sovereign with 95.1% debt-to-GDP and the widest gilt-Bund spread since the 2022 mini-Budget against a AAA/Aaa sovereign with the lowest net debt-to-GDP in the G7 — and the base leg carries an acute dated fiscal event on 2026-10-28.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The sovereign-credit differential in this cross is unusually stark and both bond markets are pricing it while neither currency fully is. The UK is rated AA (S&P) and AA- (Fitch), Moody's reported variously as Aa2 or Aa3 with no confirmable outlook, carries public sector net debt of 95.1% of GDP at end-May 2026 — highest since the early 1960s — and its ten-year gilt closed at 5.16% on 2026-08-28, highest since May 2026, at approximately 184bp over Bunds, still the widest since the 2022 mini-Budget. Canada is AAA at S&P, Aaa at Moody's and AAA at DBRS with AA+ from Fitch, one of only two AAA-rated G7 sovereigns, its ten-year is 3.74% and thirty-year 4.15% against a UK 30-year of 5.73-5.76%, and its Q2 saw a record C$80.8bn of foreign purchases of government bonds with the budget balance improving to -0.37 y/y from -1.36. The transmission is the base dossier's own regime-dependent correlation: cable against the 30-year gilt yield is normally positive but turns negative in a fiscal crisis, and a long yield entrenched within 5bp of a multi-decade peak is the crisis configuration. On the quote side there is no equivalent channel — record foreign sovereign demand is the opposite of an auction-stress environment.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Strategically this is the second-strongest bearish leg after terms of trade, because the base leg's fiscal arithmetic is closed and adverse while the quote leg's is improving. The OBR's March 2026 spring forecast left the Chancellor GBP 9.9bn of headroom, a margin the OBR itself warned could be wiped out by a modest rise in borrowing costs, with roughly GBP 3bn reported lost to gilt moves by 20 March; since then the ten-year has risen a further 39bp year on year and the 30-year has settled within 5bp of its multi-decade peak, so at roughly GBP 2.5bn of extra annual debt service per 0.25pp the March headroom has plausibly been consumed entirely. That leaves the Chancellor three options on 2026-10-28 — tax rises, spending cuts or a rule change — and the gilt market will not tolerate the third. Canada by contrast revised its 2025-26 deficit down to C$66.9bn, is being funded by record foreign sovereign demand, and is being assessed by agencies on effective and predictable policymaking with no rating action pending. The one Canadian fiscal risk worth naming is the open-ended tariff support package Carney has committed to for as long as it takes — an uncapped commitment against a shrinking tariff-exposed tax base — but that is a AAA sovereign taking on a contingent liability, not a AA sovereign with no headroom facing a dated forecast round.

Tactically the UK fiscal premium is a standing condition already visible in the gilt curve but with no scheduled catalyst to convert it into a currency move, while the Canadian sovereign carries no tactical event at all. Strategically 2026-10-28 is that catalyst, and it lands with the OBR's March headroom almost certainly consumed, which is why confidence rises with the horizon rather than falling.

catalysts.event: Bank of Canada policy decision, statement and Governor's press conference
catalysts.rationale: The rate outcome is a non-event for the pair — a 3% hike probability and all 35 Reuters-polled economists at hold means the 150bp differential enters and leaves this meeting unchanged. The tradeable content is Macklem's tone on whether the balance of risks has shifted toward oil-driven inflation or tariff-driven growth weakness, and because the Canadian curve carries roughly 65% of a 2026 hike while sterling's curve prices nothing until 2027, a hawkish tone extends Canadian pricing and pushes the pair lower while a dovish tone begins marking it out and lifts the pair. This is the first of the two banks to speak in each round, setting the frame for the 2026-09-17 MPC.

catalysts.event: Canada merchandise trade balance (July) and Q2 labour productivity; UK final composite and services PMI for August
catalysts.rationale: Canadian consensus of C$3.2bn against a C$3.86bn prior implies the market expects immediate tariff drag, but July data predate the 2026-08-22 Section 338 duties entirely and energy — explicitly carved out — was priced at elevated crude through the month, so the timing mismatch argues for a beat. The UK final PMIs are a confirmation of a flash that already beat on composite and services, carrying little news unless services is revised below 52.0. A Canadian beat against a UK non-event pushes the pair lower, most likely into the 200-day average at 1.86002.

catalysts.event: Canada Labour Force Survey (August) and Ivey PMI; BoE Governor Bailey speaks; CFTC positioning release for both legs
catalysts.rationale: Canadian consensus is +15.8k employment with unemployment steady at 6.4% after July's +75.1k and a third consecutive decline, a bar lowered enough that Ontario momentum argues for a beat. Bailey's first scheduled remarks since the 29 July minutes matter because he has argued the upward-sloping gilt curve is itself weighing on inflation pressures — any elaboration that the fiscal premium substitutes for a hike is directly sterling-negative. The same-day CFTC release shows whether the six-to-one covering asymmetry between the two legs is still running.

catalysts.event: Canada's retaliatory tariffs take effect on approximately US$20bn of US goods at rates of 15-50%
catalysts.rationale: The only genuinely unpriced dated binary on either leg inside the tactical window, because the product-level list had not been published at the valuation date, so the market cannot have discounted its composition or the probability of further US escalation in response. Dollar-for-dollar retaliation is proportionally heavier on an economy roughly one tenth the size of its counterpart, and Carney called the step reluctant precisely because it raises Canadian costs and reduces choice. A broader-than-trailed list is quote-negative and lifts the pair toward the resistance band; a narrow one resolves the uncertainty and opens the 200-day.

catalysts.event: UK monthly GDP, trade balance, industrial and manufacturing production for July
catalysts.rationale: The trade balance is the first hard read on whether the energy import bill is showing through into the goods deficit, which is the direct measurement of the terms-of-trade channel that carries the largest strategic weight in this analysis. A widening deficit alongside soft monthly GDP would corroborate the income-transfer thesis at exactly the moment Canada is posting a record current account surplus on the other side.

catalysts.event: Statistics Canada Consumer Price Index for August
catalysts.rationale: The most important quote-leg data point of the tactical window and a genuine two-way risk for the pair. Priors are headline 3.0%, CPI-trim 1.9% and CPI-median 2.0%, with the entire headline-core gap attributable to gasoline up 25.7% year on year. If CPI-trim rises toward 2.2-2.5% Canadian hike pricing extends and the pair falls toward the eight-touch shelf; if trim slips below 1.9% the statistical basis for a 2026 hike disappears and the pair is supported back into the resistance band.

catalysts.event: UK labour market report: unemployment rate, claimant count, average weekly earnings
catalysts.rationale: Priors are unemployment 4.9%, regular pay 3.5% with the private sector at only 2.8%, and payrolled employees down 210,000 on the year. This release most directly determines whether the Bank of England's hawkish tail — the three standing votes for 4.00% that underpin sterling's 150bp advantage — survives. Further loosening undermines the one clearly bullish leg of the strategic analysis, the base-leg mirror of the 2026-09-14 Canadian CPI.

catalysts.event: UK August CPI, core CPI, services CPI and RPI; FOMC decision with Summary of Economic Projections
catalysts.rationale: The densest day of the tactical window for the base leg. UK headline was 2.9% with core 2.6% and services 3.4%, and the August print carries genuine upside risk from gas running 18-21% above the Bank's conditioning assumption plus BRC shop prices at a two-year high of 1.5%. A hot print is doubly ambiguous: it raises odds the BoE defends 3.75% (pair-positive) while deepening the real-income and terms-of-trade tax (pair-negative). The FOMC matters less here than for either currency alone since both legs lose the same 25bp to the dollar and only the beta differential survives.

catalysts.event: Bank of England MPC decision and minutes, plus the annual vote on the next twelve-month gilt reduction pace
catalysts.rationale: Roughly +7bp is priced and 56 of 64 economists expect no change, so the rate outcome is close to fully discounted and the information sits in the vote split and the QT decision. A split moving from 6-3 to 7-2 thins the hawkish tail supporting sterling's differential; a move to 5-4 would force a repricing of a 2026 hike back in and lift the pair through the resistance band toward the unmapped void. The annual QT vote is a gilt-supply event with a currency consequence through the fiscal-premium channel.

catalysts.event: Canada Consumer Price Index for September (indicative date, not in gated calendar)
catalysts.rationale: The first Canadian CPI in which the gasoline base effect turns materially less favourable and the first to capture tariff pass-through. Headline should converge down toward the 2.0% core average, removing the statistical support for roughly 65% of a 2026 hike and leaving the 150bp differential intact — the mechanism by which the largest positive contribution in the strategic score is realised, and pair-supportive.

catalysts.event: UK Autumn Budget with OBR economic and fiscal forecast AND Bank of Canada decision with Monetary Policy Report — both on the same day
catalysts.rationale: The defining date for this cross and the reason strategic conviction is 2 rather than 3, because it tests both legs of the analysis simultaneously in opposite directions. The Budget asks whether a gilt market charging 184bp over Bunds, with the OBR's March GBP 9.9bn headroom plausibly consumed, converts a sovereign risk premium into a currency premium — pair-negative if it does. The Monetary Policy Report asks whether the BoC can defend roughly 65% of a hike in a forecast round that must mark down growth for tariffs and inflation for gasoline base effects — pair-positive if it cannot. The pair's own 94.7-day estimated implied vol charges almost nothing for this collision, and with no listed option there is no cheap way to cap the resulting gap.

The only dated circuit-breaker for the US-Canada trade conflict inside the strategic horizon, and Ottawa's own internal assessment is that no substantive talks resume before it. Section 338 duties are removable by presidential proclamation with no statutory process, so a credible post-midterm restart reprices the entire Canadian tariff premium in a single move rather than gradually, which would be quote-positive and pull the pair lower.

catalysts.event: Bank of England MPC decision with Monetary Policy Report
catalysts.rationale: The base leg's answer to the Canadian Monetary Policy Report eight days earlier, and the first full sterling forecast round after the Budget. The three standing hawks vote again with 2027 pay settlement evidence beginning to arrive, and incoming evidence leans dovish with private-sector regular pay at 2.8% and DMP three-year CPI expectations at 2.8%. A dovish resolution removes the hawkish tail supporting sterling's differential (pair-negative); a hike to 4.00% would widen the differential to 175bp and is the single largest pair-positive event available in the horizon.

The final Canadian decision of 2026 and the terminal date for the market's roughly 65% year-end hike probability. If the Bank has not moved by this meeting the entire 2026 hike premium is removed from the Canadian curve, leaving the 150bp differential intact against a forward curve that had priced compression — the direct realisation of the largest positive contribution in the strategic score.

The meeting at which the Committee expects to have learned about 2027 pay settlements, the input the July minutes name as decisive. If private-sector regular pay is still near 2.8% and unemployment above 5.0%, the dovish resolution arrives here and sterling's differential over Canada becomes a shrinking asset rather than a stable one, which is pair-negative. It falls eight days after the Canadian decision on 2026-12-09, repeating the sequencing pattern.

catalysts.event: United States tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks, automotive parts and steel rise to 50%
catalysts.rationale: A dated, pre-announced escalation just beyond the strategic horizon that extends the tariff regime from US$20bn and 5.2% of bilateral exports to a materially larger share, striking the auto sector that drove Canadian Q2 growth. Because Section 338 carries no expiry it persists until a presidential proclamation removes it — quote-negative and pair-positive, and the principal reason the Canadian speculative short may deepen rather than resolve.

This is pass 2 of 2. All ten factor stances, confidences, evidence_type labels, weights, weighted contributions, net scores, convictions, score interpretations, rationales, G10 rankings and cross-horizon consistency text are reproduced unchanged from the pass-1 verdict, scored without the price payload by design. Weight adjustments: five factors adjusted, each within the ±0.05 limit, each summing to exactly 1.00, each documented with a specific bilateral reason. The two largest adjustments — External Balance up 0.03 on both horizons and USD Liquidity down 0.04 on both — follow the framework's own illustrative patterns for commodity-versus-non-commodity pairs and non-USD crosses respectively.

Bilateral trade: taken directly from the injected IMF DOTS block (UK exports to Canada US$8.9bn, imports US$8.4bn in 2024, US$0.5bn UK net surplus), not re-estimated from the web. A reporter asymmetry is disclosed (Canada reports US$20.6bn of exports to the UK against US$7.3bn of imports, a gold-routing artefact) and not reconciled; UK-reported figures are used for the base-leg perspective. The bilateral channel is immaterial and not treated as a pair driver.

Consensus forecasts: pass 1 correctly recorded bank_consensus_forecast as null; pass-2 research surfaced two usable secondary aggregations and one brokerage outlook, all labelled best available rather than primary bank research. Extrapolation-script venues (LongForecast, WalletInvestor, CoinCodex, 30rates, Traders Union) were excluded as a category error, not weighted as weak sources.

Chart patterns sourced from the web (TradingView community ideas, technical-analysis blogs, an Elliott Wave site) carry weak provenance and are explicitly subordinated to the payload's computed zones with stated touch counts wherever the two disagree; one direct conflict (a June 2026 note describing 1.87 as an unbroken ceiling) is resolved in favour of the payload, which shows sustained closes above 1.87 and a 1.90211 closing high on 6 July.

Positioning vintages and taxonomies differ between legs: the sterling figure is the legacy non-commercial net from the 2026-08-28 release (data to 25 August); the Canadian figure is the disaggregated leveraged-fund plus asset-manager net at the 2026-08-25 reference date. These are not directly comparable in level; the pair inference rests on percentile standing and rate of change, both dossier estimates against trailing tranche series.

Valuation uses relative BIS REERs (June 2026) as a labelled proxy, not a PPP fair-value source. The implied 1.6167 REER-equalisation level is arithmetic, not a target. The June reference month is approximately 63 days from the valuation date, marginally outside the 60-day strategic freshness window.

Documented gaps specific to this cross: no GBP/CAD listed option and therefore no quoted implied volatility, risk reversal, butterfly or skew; no quoted forward points; no one-year implied-volatility percentile; no quoted GBP/CAD cross-currency basis; no primary bank forecast survey; and fewer than three computed resistance zones, requiring supplementation with round numbers and the 52-week high.
